When speaking with an older adult who has hearing loss, speaking a little slower than normal can help with comprehension, but shouting or speaking loudly into one ear may distort sound and isn’t recommended.  
Facing them so they can see your lips allows them to use visual cues (lip reading and facial expressions), which improves understanding.  
Asking another person to translate is unnecessary in most cases and may undermine the person’s independence.  
Best practice in communication with hearing-impaired older adults includes facing the person directly and speaking clearly without exaggerating.  

Final answer: (C)
